text: All leads (L1 through L6) were verified as accurate security issues in the respective files (Dockerfile and app.py). We read Dockerfile, app.py, and README.md.

findings.title: Running container as root user
findings.explanation: The Dockerfile runs the container process as the root user by default because no USER instruction is specified before CMD.
findings.fix: Add a non-root user and switch to it using USER nonrootuser before running CMD.
findings.description: The Dockerfile runs the container process as the root user by default because no USER instruction is specified before CMD.

findings.title: SQL Injection in login form
findings.explanation: User-controlled input from request.form is directly interpolated into a SQL query string and executed via sqlite3 cursor.execute(), allowing SQL injection.
findings.fix: Use parameterized queries with placeholder '?' instead of string formatting.
findings.evidence: f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE username='{username}' AND password='{password}'"
findings.description: User-controlled input from request.form is directly interpolated into a SQL query string and executed via sqlite3 cursor.execute(), allowing SQL injection.
findings.code:
# Vulnerable SQL query construction (intentional)
        sql_query = (
            f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE username='{username}' AND password='{password}'"
        )

findings.title: Flask Debug Mode Enabled and Bound to 0.0.0.0
findings.explanation: Flask app runs with debug=True and binds to all interfaces (0.0.0.0), which exposes the interactive debugger and leaks sensitive info if deployed to production.
findings.fix: Disable debug mode and bind only to localhost or use a production WSGI server.
findings.description: Flask app runs with debug=True and binds to all interfaces (0.0.0.0), which exposes the interactive debugger and leaks sensitive info if deployed to production.
